activity.message:
Open a licence text from its row

Tapping a row in Settings > Licences left a blank page: a value-based link had no destination it could use, because the
Settings sheet already reaches this screen through its own link. Each row now carries its own destination.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Stop tracking the private label file

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Document third-party material, privacy and the use of AI

THIRD_PARTY.md lists what ships and what only builds or tests, with licences, and says that no copyleft or
non-commercial licence is used. PRIVACY.md says what stays on the phone and lists every network address in the code. The
README gains permissions, installation, licence and the AI-assistance statement. data-sources.md notes the clause that
makes the city the owner of derived data, compared again with the feed's terms of use.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Show the licence of everything the app contains, inside the app

BSD and Apache licences require their text to come with a binary. Settings > Licences lists MapLibre Native,
SwiftProtobuf, the GTFS Realtime definition, ZIPFoundation, Noto Sans and the Protomaps styles with their full
licence texts (bundled as App/Resources/Licenses/*.txt), the OpenStreetMap and City of Madison credits, and the
app's own MIT licence. A test checks that every entry's text is in the app.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Name the copyright holder in full, in LICENSE and in the app's Info.plist

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Open the history behind a punctuality bar, fix the squeezed bus counts, and tidy the tiles, credits and favourite stops

Touching a punctuality bar under "Usually at this stop" opens a screen with hour-by-hour charts for weekdays, Saturdays
or Sundays (this stop or the whole route): the share of early, on-time and late arrivals, and the spread from the
timetable. The bus counts beside a route are coloured numbers (red, green, blue) instead of numbers in capsules, which
were squeezed on a real phone. The first and last stop of a route are purple and black (white on the dark map) so that
they differ from the lateness colours. The three tiles on the service board are equal squares across the full width.
Favourite stops are solid dots instead of an orange ring. The map credits sit level with each other, lower and in from
the corners of a rounded screen. Version 0.5.1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Colour the buses of each route by lateness, mark buses that are not on a trip, ring first and last stops, and open the live bar

Lateness: the routes list, the route chooser and the chip over the map count the buses of a route, of each direction and of
each destination, and colour them red (over 5 min late), green (on time) or blue (over 2 min early); routes with an alert
get a triangle. A bus's sheet says how far it is from its timetable and what trip it runs next. The live bar over the map
opens a card with the same for the whole network and a refresh button. Settings > Times is one choice: off, minutes, or
minutes with the timetable's time; the last leads the stop board with the timetable's time and puts the live countdown
under it.

Buses that are not on a trip (5 to 7 of about 125) are pale with an orange ring and "!", or show the route they will run
next and when, from the trip updates. A route in focus rings its first stop green and its last red, labelled D1/D2 where a
direction has several destinations.

Also: the service info summary is three square tiles with the number under the symbol, the map credits sit lower and in
from the corners on phones with rounded screens, and feedanalysis gets `fleet` and `layover`. Version 0.5.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make the launch five times faster, and add destination focus, back to list and scheduled times beside live ones

Launch: slides between lanes were cut into pieces of a few metres, so the saved map data held 90 000 line pieces and
13 MB. Slides now go in steps of an eighth of a lane and one route, and every line is thinned to 1 m: 23 000 pieces and
3 MB, and the saved data is read and drawn in 0.5 s instead of 2.5 s on a Mac.

Focus: the chip over the map opens its choices from anywhere on it and lists the destinations of each direction (D1,
D2, ...); one can be shown on its own (line, stops, buses). "Show on map" from the service info or the routes list leaves
a back button. A journey is drawn on the map only while its steps are open.

Times: a live bus keeps its timetable time (stop board, next stops, full timetable with +3 / -2 marks); a setting turns
it off. Also: the routes list shows the bus count beside each name, the service info chips wrap and say which ones are
buttons, the status pill stays on one line, the map credits sit in from the screen corners, and the buses and route
lines are smaller when zoomed out. Version 0.4.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Update the test count in the README

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Show each bus's direction as a letter and a white or black ring, and shrink markers and lines with zoom

The heading arrow is gone: it ignored the route focus and the feed's bearing changes at every turn. A bus now shows
the way its trip runs ("E", "W", "N", "S", "In", "Out") from the feed's trip_direction_name, and a white ring for
direction 1 or a black one for direction 0. Bus markers, route lines, lane gaps and journey lines are smaller on the
whole-city view and reach full size at zoom 15 and 16. Version 0.3.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
